title: How to Play With Ideas Using Computer Simulations: A Gentle Introduction to Computational Modeling via Systems Dynamics
titleZh: 如何用计算机模拟玩转想法：通过系统动力学进行计算建模的入门简介
abstract: Computational modeling provides a way to translate theory into explicit representations that can be simulated and examined, but many researchers lack a clear entry point for doing so. In this article, I introduce a two-step procedure designed especially for psychologists, particularly psychologists with little or no programming experience, who are interested in exploring computational modeling but are unsure how to start. The procedure involves two steps: (a) converting box-and-arrow diagrams (which many psychologists are already familiar with) into stock-and-flow (SF) diagrams and then (b) developing pseudocode from the SF diagram. Once these steps are completed, translating the model into executable syntax becomes straightforward. The goal is not to teach programming or simulation in depth but to show how conceptual models can be expressed in a form precise enough to generate trajectories over time. I then describe why this translation matters for theory. Explicit computational representations allow researchers to compare alternative explanations, evaluate whether simpler mechanisms are sufficient to reproduce observed patterns, examine whether theories generate the outcomes they claim, and explore ideas or policies that would be difficult to test directly in the field. Ready-to-use R code is provided to support hands-on learning to reach the broader aim of making computational modeling a practical and approachable tool for psychologists interested in evaluating their theories with computational modeling.

journal.name: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
